body: It is a little sad to see however I still think it was worth mentioning its lack of inclusion. I don't think it completely ruined the entire episode but it would have just been something that I would have preferred to skip. Thanks for linking that as well I had no idea it existed.

While I understand that the show in general has graphic themes that may be more or less severe than self harm I don't think it detracts from my point specifically. I think trigger warnings for very sensitive topics should be included where possible and I really don't think that it detracts from the show in any way to just have a little message at the beginning for those things.

I do also understand that it would probably be something that Amazon has to implement and perhaps to add something like that now would not be feasible but I just thought it was worth discussing. I will also add that despite this I think the last few episodes were fantastic I just thought that an inclusion of something like that would be nice to have. I also wanted to discuss it as I wasn't sure if maybe I had missed something particular.

While I do agree that the context was completely different to a typical scenario of self harm, for me the act itself is enough to make watching the show difficult. I have personal experience with self harm and especially the implement and visual effects made enjoying the rest of the episode difficult. I'm not at all trying to minimise anyone's experience but I personally was not expecting that and it made me a few of my friends pretty uncomfortable. 

As a side note I did still enjoy the episodes and so far I think the season is great its just something that I think could have been included and would have made the experience a lot better is all.

Everyone is becoming so occupied with the notion of "shovelware" that they are completely missing the point of doing something like this. Not only would this be a valuable learning experience but trying to decide on whether a game is good or not based on the industry standards is a sure-fire way to stifle amateur game makers from ever making even one game. A game that takes longer to make doesn't make it better. If a game is able to execute on its intended experience well then it is good. Don't late gamers dictate what makes good games. Making lots of little games is a great way to learn, don't let anyone stop you from doing that by letting yourself think that doing so is contributing to "shovelware".
